narrative.overview:
OCBC Verify is a deep-navy shell on a cool off-white ground, and its judgement is staged. Whenever a payment, a call or a message is risky, the app answers on a large rounded stage: a scanning ring and a big "Checking…", then a full-strength colour field sweeps in from the left, a round seal stamps down and a display-weight verdict rises. The verdict can be read from the back of a room on a projector, and also by a 68-year-old customer who is being coached over the phone.

The rest of the system stays quiet so the stage carries the weight. Surfaces are white cards with soft, navy-tinted depth. Colour is rationed by meaning, and every hue does one job: orange is the only action colour, green means verified, red means scam or risk, amber means caution, and navy is the shell. Actions are pills, panels have 20px corners, and the type pairs Bricolage Grotesque for verdicts, headings and money with Figtree for everything people read.

Density follows the person. Customer screens are one calm column with 52px actions and generous gaps, and they grow further in Easy Mode (20px base text, 60px buttons, 1.5rem gaps). The staff console runs the same tokens tighter: a navy rail, a stat strip and a sortable table.
keyCharacteristics: Deep blue-navy shell: header, hero bands, the paused stage, the staff rail and the disclaimer strip.
Full-bleed verdict fields in strong green, red and amber, each with its own AA text colour.
Vivid orange pill buttons with navy text as the single call to action.
Bricolage Grotesque at extrabold weight for verdicts and money; Figtree for body text.
Two soft shadow levels, both tinted from the navy.
rem-based sizing everywhere, so Easy Mode and the text-size setting scale the whole UI.
Motion that tells the story (sweep, stamp, rise) and becomes plain fades under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Every hue has exactly one meaning: orange is action, green is verified, red is scam or risk, amber is caution, navy is the shell. Orange never signals a warning, and green never decorates.

rules.name: The Ink, Soft, Strong Rule
rules.body: A signal colour appears in only three forms: ink (text and icons on light), soft (a tinted chip or banner behind foreground text) and strong (a full verdict field). A strong field always takes its matching on-colour.

rules.name: The Navy-on-Bright Rule
rules.body: Orange, green and amber fills carry navy text. White text appears only on the navy shell, on navy-fill and on danger-strong.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Components never write raw hex. Every colour comes from a CSS variable in tokens.css through the Tailwind preset, and dark mode and Easy Mode work by redefining those variables.

rules.name: The Stage Voice Rule
rules.body: Extrabold Bricolage belongs to verdicts, money and the hero heading. Ordinary headings stay at bold, so the stage is always the loudest thing on screen.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every amount uses tabular figures and is written in full ("S$1,500"), so columns align and digits never jump.

rules.name: The One Ramp Rule
rules.body: There is a single rem-based scale (0.8125, 0.875, 1, 1.125, 1.375, 1.75, 2.25, 3, 3.75rem). Nothing is sized in px, so the browser's text size, the app's four text sizes and Easy Mode all scale it together.

rules.name: The Two Levels Rule
rules.body: Only card and lift exist. Anything that interrupts (a stage, a dialog, a toast) gets lift, and everything else gets card or no shadow.

rules.name: The Pill Action Rule
rules.body: If it is a button, it is a pill. Corners of 20px are for things that hold content, and 14px is for things you type into or pick from.

dos: **Do** resolve every risky moment on the Verdict Stage: a navy checking state, then a full strong-colour field with a round seal and an extrabold Bricolage title.
**Do** put navy text on orange, green and amber fills, and reserve white text for navy, navy-fill and danger-strong.
**Do** keep the verdict in the DOM and visible by default, and hold the actions after the stage (`[data-stage-running] ~ *`, `data-after-stage`) until it settles.
**Do** set money in Bricolage extrabold with tabular figures, written in full ("S$1,500").
**Do** size type and spacing in rem from the one ramp so Easy Mode (20px base, 60px buttons, 1.5rem gaps) scales the whole interface.
**Do** give every pressable control at least 44px, and primary actions and inputs 52px.
**Do** pair every signal colour with an icon and words in chips, banners, reason lists and stages, so meaning never rests on colour alone.
**Do** let Noto Sans SC and Noto Sans Tamil lead the font stacks in Chinese and Tamil, with display letter-spacing at 0.
**Do** keep the navy disclaimer strip at the top of every screen.
donts: **Don't** use orange for anything other than action and brand: no orange warnings, and no orange text on light surfaces except accent-ink.
**Don't** put white text on the green or amber strong fields.
**Don't** use the shield-check seal as the brand or for anything but a verified state. The brand is the "V" monogram and the pause uses a hand.
**Don't** write raw hex in components; every colour comes through a token variable.
**Don't** add shadow levels beyond card and lift, or hard offset shadows.
**Don't** animate with `transition: all` or background-position shimmer. Animate only transform and opacity.
**Don't** move or scale anything under reduced motion. Use fades only and stop loops.
